section: National income concepts - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, factor cost vs market price, GVA, deflator
subsections: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s: If the GDP at market prices of an economy is ₹500 crore and its Net Factor Income from Abroad is –₹10 crore, the GNP at market prices will be
accepted.x: GNP at market prices = GDP at market prices + NFIA. Therefore, GNP = ₹500 crore – ₹10 crore = ₹490 crore.
accepted.tq: Apply the domestic-to-national conversion formula and retain the sign of NFIA.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding national income aggregates:
1. NDP is obtained by deducting depreciation from GDP.
2. NNP is obtained by deducting depreciation from GNP.
3. NNP at factor cost is the standard measure of national income.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. NDP = GDP – depreciation, NNP = GNP – depreciation, and NNP at factor cost is National Income.
accepted.tq: Check each conversion separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s: Why is depreciation deducted while calculating net national or domestic product?
o: Because depreciation measures the income earned by foreign factors
Because depreciation is a direct tax on capital goods
Because depreciation represents transfer payments to households
Because output used merely to replace worn-out capital does not constitute new output
accepted.x: Depreciation, or consumption of fixed capital, is deducted because production used only to replace worn-out capital adds nothing new to the productive stock.
accepted.tq: Identify the economic purpose of the gross-to-net adjustment.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s: A country has GDP at market prices of ₹500 crore, depreciation of ₹50 crore, NFIA of –₹10 crore and net indirect taxes of ₹40 crore. Its national income is
accepted.x: GNPMP = 500 – 10 = ₹490 crore; NNPMP = 490 – 50 = ₹440 crore; NNPFC = 440 – 40 = ₹400 crore. NNP at factor cost is national income.
accepted.tq: Perform the conversions in sequence: domestic, national, gross, net and market price to factor cost.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. National income is measured over a period of time.
2. National wealth is measured at a point of time.
3. National income is a stock concept, whereas national wealth is a flow concept.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: National income is a flow measured per year, while national wealth is a stock measured at a point of time. Statement 3 reverses these concepts.
accepted.tq: Use the flow-versus-stock distinction to reject the reversed statement.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)?
o: Exports minus imports of goods and services
Domestic factor income minus domestic consumption
Factor income paid abroad minus factor income received from abroad
Factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad
accepted.x: NFIA is factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad. It is added to GDP to obtain GNP.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between income flows and trade flows.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s: Indians earn ₹20 crore abroad and foreigners earn ₹10 crore within India. If India's GDP at market prices is ₹110 crore, its GNP at market prices is
accepted.x: NFIA = ₹20 crore – ₹10 crore = ₹10 crore. Hence, GNP = GDP + NFIA = ₹110 crore + ₹10 crore = ₹120 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate income earned by nationals abroad from income earned by foreigners domestically.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s: Income earned by an Indian resident working in Saudi Arabia is included in
o: India's GNP but not its GDP
India's GDP but not its GNP
neither India's GDP nor its GNP
accepted.x: GDP is based on production within domestic territory, whereas GNP includes the income of nationals or normal residents wherever located.
accepted.tq: Distinguish territorial residence from nationality or normal residence.
accepted.sec: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

accepted.s: The value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a country during a year, irrespective of who produces them, is called
accepted.x: GDP measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a country's geographical boundaries during a year, including production by residents and non-residents.
accepted.tq: Match the territorial definition with the correct aggregate.
accepted.sec: Definitions - stem to term

accepted.s: GDP can be expressed as Q × P because it represents
o: the quantity of intermediate goods multiplied by their factor cost
the quantity of exports multiplied by the exchange rate
the population multiplied by per capita income
the quantity of final output multiplied by its price
accepted.x: GDP is the market value of final output, represented as quantity of output (Q) multiplied by its price (P).
accepted.tq: Translate the compact formula into its economic meaning.
accepted.sec: Definitions - stem to term

accepted.s: The ratio of national income to population is referred to as
accepted.x: Per capita income is calculated as national income divided by population.
accepted.tq: Identify the term from its defining ratio.
accepted.sec: Definitions - stem to term

accepted.s: Wages, rent, interest and profit earned by the factors of production together constitute
accepted.x: Factor income consists of payments to factors of production: wages, rent, interest and profit.
accepted.tq: Match each factor payment with the umbrella concept.
accepted.sec: Definitions - stem to term

accepted.s: GDP at factor cost is obtained from GDP at market prices by
o: subtracting indirect taxes and adding subsidies
subtracting direct taxes and adding exports
adding indirect taxes and subtracting subsidies
accepted.x: GDPFC = GDPMP – indirect taxes + subsidies. Direct taxes, depreciation and NFIA are not the bridging items in this conversion.
accepted.tq: Remember the direction of the market-price-to-factor-cost adjustment.
accepted.sec: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about prices used in national accounts:
1. Market price equals factor cost plus indirect taxes minus subsidies.
2. GDP at factor cost equals GDP at market prices minus indirect taxes plus subsidies.
3. Direct taxes are the bridging item between GDP at market prices and GDP at factor cost.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 correctly state the conversion. Statement 3 is false because indirect taxes and subsidies, not direct taxes, form the relevant bridge.
accepted.tq: Use the sign convention and eliminate the statement naming the wrong tax category.
accepted.sec: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

accepted.s: Which of the following is a production tax rather than a product tax?
o: Sales tax on each unit sold
Excise duty per unit of output
accepted.x: Production taxes are levied irrespective of the quantity of output; stamp duty and property tax are examples. GST, excise and sales tax are product taxes levied per unit or value of product.
accepted.tq: Use the test of whether the levy varies with the quantity of output.
accepted.sec: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

accepted.s: A tax imposed per unit of a commodity, such as GST, excise duty or sales tax, is classified as
accepted.x: Product taxes are levied on a unit or value of a product. Production taxes such as stamp duty and property tax are imposed irrespective of output.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar tax terms using their basis of levy.
accepted.sec: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

accepted.s:
With reference to GVA, consider the following statements:
1. GVA at basic prices has been the headline sectoral measure since the 2011-12 series.
2. GVA includes depreciation.
3. NVA excludes depreciation.
4. GVA at basic prices is not used in the 2022-23 series.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. GVA at basic prices continues to be used in the 2022-23 series, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Combine the time-series fact with the gross-versus-net distinction and reject the reversed date claim.
accepted.sec: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

accepted.s: The headline growth measure used by the CSO/NSO for sectoral growth is based on
accepted.x: CSO/NSO headline sectoral growth is based on GVA at basic prices.
accepted.tq: Identify the official headline aggregate rather than the national-income aggregate.
accepted.sec: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

accepted.s: In Q1 of 2026-27, real GDP was ₹81.36 lakh crore and real GVA was ₹73.82 lakh crore. The difference primarily represents
accepted.x: The difference between GDP and GVA at the relevant price level is attributable to net product taxes. Here the difference is ₹7.54 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Interpret the gap between GDP and GVA through the product-tax bridge.
accepted.sec: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses National Income?
o: NNP at market prices + net indirect taxes
NNP at factor cost = net domestic factor income + NFIA
NDP at market prices – depreciation – NFIA
GDP at market prices – NFIA + depreciation
accepted.x: National Income is NNP at factor cost. It equals net domestic factor income plus NFIA and represents factor incomes of the country's normal residents.
accepted.tq: Start with the standard aggregate and verify its factor-income components.
accepted.sec: National income - the standard aggregate

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations represents the components of national income at factor cost?
o: Indirect taxes, subsidies, depreciation and exports
Consumption, investment, government expenditure and imports
Wages, rent, interest and profits earned by the country's normal residents
Only wages and salaries earned within domestic territory
accepted.x: National income is the sum of wages, rent, interest and profits earned by factors belonging to the country, including the adjustment for NFIA.
accepted.tq: Match the factor-payment composition with the standard aggregate.
accepted.sec: National income - the standard aggregate
